title: Knitting on two circular needles
subtitle: An alternative to DPNs for small circumferences using two full-length circulars.
excerpt: Working on two circular needles divides the stitches between two separate cables, each needle working its own half of the round. Some knitters find this more intuitive than magic loop or DPNs.
sourceNotes: Method widely used in modern knitting practice as an alternative to DPNs and magic loop. Consistent with the two-cable circular mechanics described in mid-twentieth-century British knitting handbooks.

glossaryTerms.definition: A technique for knitting small circumferences in the round using two separate circular needles. Half the stitches live on each cable, and each needle works its own half in turn.

content.text: Working on two circular needles distributes the stitches equally between two cables. Each needle works only its own half: when needle A is active, needle B hangs from its cable behind the work; when needle B is active, needle A hangs. The result is the same fabric as DPNs or magic loop, but with no ladder risk at junctions (because there are only two junctions rather than four or five) and no cable-loop management. The
suits knitters who find the magic loop rotation confusing. Difficulty: intermediate.
Two circular needles of the same size (40-60 cm works well; longer cables are fine)
Yarn in a quantity to suit your project
Cast all stitches onto needle A.
Slide half the stitches from needle A onto needle B (the left tip of needle B).
Arrange both needles so the cast-on edge faces the same direction on both cables. Check for twists.
To begin, work the stitches on needle A: slide the right tip of needle A under the left tip so needle A is in working position. Knit across all needle A stitches using the right tip of needle A.
Rotate the work so needle B faces you. Repeat: slide the right tip of needle B into position and knit across all needle B stitches. One full round completed.

Sock knitters who prefer a shorter cable to the magic loop like two circulars. It also suits knitting two identical items at once: two socks, two sleeves. Each needle holds one item; you work each in turn.

items.symptom: Accidentally worked stitches off the wrong needle
items.cause: Using the wrong needle tip to knit; the inactive needle tip drifted into working position
items.fix: Before beginning each half-round, identify which cable is active by looking at where the working yarn is. The active needle is always the one connected to the working yarn.

items.symptom: Ladder at the join between needles
items.fix: At the start of each needle, work the first two stitches snugly before settling to normal tension.
